games.title: Dilorias rings the f2 doorbell
games.capsule: The first queen exit drags the white king to f2. The continuation brings the black h-rook to g2 with check, but the recorded finish is White’s 33.Qxd7#.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: Pause the film. From d5, Dilorias can take the rook on h1: the diagonal is d5–e4–f3–g2–h1. The deeper search finds 4...Qxh1. There was treasure before the smoke bomb.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: Doorbell! I have arrived on f2 carrying a check and absolutely no return ticket.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: The recorded reply is Kxf2. Nxf2 was also legal. The queen bought a pawn and a question for the king; she did not force this particular king move.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: A rook reaches g2 with check. The understudies have found the spotlight. White can answer Kxg2, so this is another offering, not a trapped king.

beats.speaker: Emanuel
beats.text: The night begins with a queen sacrifice and ends with checkmate against us. Keep both pictures: the imaginative opening and the actual last square.

games.title: The bishop behind the smoke
games.capsule: Bishop shuttles invite ...Nxc2+. The queen takes that knight, and the bishop on f5 takes the queen. The same geometry returns in game 19.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The bishop has now traveled b2–c1–b2–c1–b2. A very busy doorway. Almost everyone else is still at home.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The queen takes the knight on c2. Trace the diagonal from f5 through e4 and d3: the bishop can reach c2.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: Exit through the bishop’s diagonal. I would like the lighting crew to remember that diagonal next time.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: The king’s long walk ends in checkmate. In the return encounter, watch the bishop and the checking knight together.

games.title: The queen offered, the queen collected
games.capsule: A five-move win with an important missing branch: after 4...Qxd3, White could have taken Manny’s queen with 5.Qxd3. Instead 5.Nf3 allowed ...Qxd1+.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: I take the bishop on d3 and stand directly in front of the other queen. This is an offer, not an invisibility spell.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: White develops the knight. The unplayed 5.Qxd3 would have captured the queen on d3. Now the d-file is open in the other direction.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: Dilorias collects the opposing queen with check. Black is awarded the game here. The board is not checkmate; the PGN says Normal and does not specify the off-board cause.

games.title: Harriet tries to light the whole file
games.capsule: A bishop, then another bishop, then a knight go toward the black king. The queens later exchange, and Black’s c-pawn becomes the decisive passer.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The bishop takes e7. Before calling it a raid, count the reply Qxe7: this visit costs a bishop.

beats.speaker: Harriet Hissindorf
beats.text: The knight goes to h7, and I am about to run up the h-file. We have excellent enthusiasm and a rather expensive entrance fee.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: This queen move captures Black’s queen with check; ...Rxg4 completes a queen exchange. It is not one of the fifteen unmatched queen departures.

beats.speaker: Emanuel
beats.text: Black’s passed c-pawn promoted on c1 before the final queen checkmate. The king attack needed a forcing continuation much earlier.

games.title: The queen takes a bishop, and the pawn answers
games.capsule: The queen-for-bishop exchange on e5 leaves White with the surviving queen. The white attack finishes on b5.

beats.speaker: Sir Banyan Blithers
beats.text: The g8 knight has reached e4, where the d3 pawn can take it. A central square is useful only if the landing survives the reply.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: I take the bishop on e5. The f4 pawn is already looking at me. We can call this a sacrifice; we must still name what it purchases.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: The white queen finds b5. A king on a5 has very little scenery left to hide behind.

games.title: JasmineKafka’s double doorway
games.capsule: Against the export’s highest-rated opponent, the queens exchange on d4 and a knight arrives on c2 with check. Black finishes with ...g6#.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The visiting queen takes the pawn on d4. After Qxd4 Nxd4 the queens are gone, but the knight now has an excellent route.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The knight check on c2 reaches the king and the a1 rook. Removing queens has not removed tactics.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: I reached h5. The pawn on g6 supplies the final check. My travel diary needs fewer destinations and more escape squares.

games.title: Alexander’s long road to b2
games.capsule: The a-pawn runs to a3 and captures on b2, while the king remains on e8. White’s queen and bishop then coordinate a compact mate.

beats.speaker: Alexander Aaronson
beats.text: I am a long way from a7, and b2 is ahead. Before cheering, look behind me: the king and back rank still need a working shelter.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: The pawn reaches b2 by capture. White answers Bxb2; the runner is gone. The open position continues.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: The queen reaches e8, supported by the bishop’s diagonal from c6. A pawn adventure and king safety belong on the same board.

games.title: The clock awards the cloak
games.capsule: A genuine clock win after a wild knight journey. The queen exchange is ordinary; at the final board Manny’s material is much reduced.

beats.speaker: Sir Banyan Blithers
beats.text: Check on d6! A knight in the middle of the palace makes everyone look up.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The bishop move lets Black exchange queens with ...Qxe3+. The scan’s stronger continuation here is 18.Ne5. The knight’s landing matters more than how spectacular the route looked.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: White wins on time. That is the result, full stop. It does not turn the final board into a won ending: Black still has two rooks, a bishop and a knight against our king and pawns.

games.title: The diagonal behind the checking queen
games.capsule: The queen checks from a4, but Black’s ...Bd7 both blocks and attacks her. The next bishop move leaves that attack unanswered.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: Check from a4. A fine entrance. The reply ...Bd7 closes the check and opens a direct line back to me.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: White takes on d3 while the bishop on d7 still attacks the queen on a4. The next recorded move is ...Bxa4.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: Black’s queen finishes on h1. After a blocked check, ask what the blocking piece now attacks.

games.title: The bare-king escape clause
games.capsule: The king tours d7–c6–b6–a7–b8 and later stands alone. A timeout draw follows: a bare black king cannot deliver mate.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: The third king move in four turns. We are taking the scenic route before the pieces have found their coats.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: The last rook offers itself on g2. Kxg2 follows. There are still black pawns to clear before the king is truly alone.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: White takes the last black pawn on a5. Black now has only a king. White still has a rook and pawns.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The PGN records a draw by Time forfeit. The bare black king cannot mate, which explains the draw if White’s time expires. We have no move-by-move clock stamps to reconstruct the final seconds.

games.title: Dilorias returns for a final flourish
games.capsule: White wins a bishop early, then both sides get chances. A queen raid and advanced g-pawn create activity before Black’s attack finishes.

beats.speaker: Emanuel
beats.text: The bishop on g4 is ours to take, and the record does take it. There are useful captures before the spectacular adventures begin.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The bishop walks onto e5, where ...Nxe5 takes it. At this position the scan prefers Nf3. More helpers would make the later queen raid less lonely.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: The king is on h3, I am on f6, and Black’s queen will arrive on h6. The checking line and my own safety are now joined.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: The white knight visited g5 and e6, and Black’s queen collected Dilorias on f6 along the way. The final checkmate is on f2.

games.title: Banyan’s fork was already glowing
games.capsule: A clock win with a wonderful missed alternative: 13...Nxf3+ would fork the king and queen. The recorded queen capture gives White a way back.

beats.speaker: Sir Banyan Blithers
beats.text: I am the knight on e5. From f3 I would check the king on e1 and attack the queen on d4. My L-shaped doorway is already open!

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The recorded move is the queen capture, not the knight check. The deeper recheck prefers ...Nxf3+. White now answers Qxe5+, removing the knight with check.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: Black wins on time after blocking the check with ...Ne7. Keep the result, and keep the unplayed fork as a little exercise.

games.title: The castle is still on the drawing board
games.capsule: White spends much of the opening building a pawn shell while Black’s queen and rooks enter. The game ends on time after a rook exchange.

beats.speaker: Ella Elouise
beats.text: By move eight, every white move has been a pawn move. The shape is memorable; the pieces still need routes into it.

beats.speaker: Castle Andora
beats.text: At last, a rook gets outside and takes on a6. There is activity, but the bishop on c6 can recapture my next c6 visit.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: Black wins on time after the rook exchange on e6. This is a useful game for trying the same shell with earlier piece development.

games.title: Harriet’s sprint past the rook alarm
games.capsule: The queens exchange and White has real chances. Later the h-pawn sprint leaves a rook on e7 available to capture.

beats.speaker: Sir Banyan Blithers
beats.text: The queens have traded, and the knight lands on c6. This position has material to work with; there is no need to create a new queen sacrifice.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: Black has just put a rook on e8, looking at the rook on e7. The recheck prefers 20.Rxd7 for White. Name the attacked rook before sending another runner.

beats.speaker: Harriet Hissindorf
beats.text: I run to h5. The next move, ...Rxe7, takes our rook. My fast legs did not turn off its alarm.

beats.speaker: Emanuel
beats.text: The g-pawn capture completes the record, followed by a Black win on time. The earlier advantage is a good place to practice keeping the whole cast involved.

games.title: The queen hears a knight coming
games.capsule: After ...e5, White has Nf6+ followed by Nxd7, taking the queen. The black king eventually reaches b1 before White mates on b2.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: The pawn move leaves the f6 knight check available. Put the line Nf6+ Kd8 Nxd7 on the physical board before pressing on.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: The knight reaches d7 and takes me. A check was the bridge; the queen capture was the destination.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: I have arrived on b1, having crossed almost the entire kingdom. The white queen closes the b2 door.

games.title: The knight who collected the back rank
games.capsule: A white knight enters e5 and keeps finding targets. It later captures on d7, f8, e6 and f8 again, including the black queen.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The opening knight returns to the center after Nf6. White can take it with cxd5; in the game White instead develops Nc3.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The knight has taken the rook on f8. Track that same knight: it will go to e6 and then return to f8 for the queen.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: Same square, second delivery. The knight had not stopped attacking simply because the previous trophy was a rook.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: White’s queen delivers mate on d8. The knight’s tour is the pattern worth carrying out of this chapter.

games.title: The knight at the castle window
games.capsule: The queens exchange early, then ...Nxc3+ gives White a decision. The king move leaves the d1 rook available to the knight.

beats.speaker: Emanuel
beats.text: This captures Black’s queen. ...exd6 then removes ours. It is a queen exchange, with a playable middlegame still to follow.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The knight on c3 checks the king on b1 and attacks the rook on d1. The scan prefers 18.bxc3, taking the checking knight.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: I step away instead, and ...Nxd1 takes the rook. The Force would have benefited from one ordinary pawn capture.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: Black’s e-pawn promoted before the final mate. A queen-free position can grow a new queen if a passer keeps moving.

games.title: The pawn knocks on d7
games.capsule: The white e-pawn takes a bishop on d7 with check after an unusual French structure. White keeps the initiative and mates on f7.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The bishop steps onto d7 while White’s pawn on e6 attacks that square. The next move is exd7+.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: The bishop is gone and the king leaves e8. The wandering begins as a response to a concrete check.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: The white queen mates on f7. Keep the pawn’s direction in view: a small piece can be the most immediate attacker.

games.title: The bishop behind the smoke, again
games.capsule: A second encounter with luha2 repeats ...Nxc2+ Qxc2 Bxc2. This time Black later gives back a queen, but retains enough activity to win on time.

beats.speaker: Sir Banyan Blithers
beats.text: Our knights have both stepped out and then back. We are demonstrating reversibility; the opponent is developing a position.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: I take on c2 again. If the bishop on f5 looks familiar, it is because we saw this doorway in game two.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The same bishop diagonal takes the queen. Repeated patterns are useful even when they are patterns we would rather change.

beats.speaker: Emanuel
beats.text: Now Black’s queen steps onto e2 with check and our knight can take it. The game still ends as a clock loss after ...Rd8, not as a neat material verdict.

games.title: A file opens under the queen
games.capsule: Black’s f-pawn capture opens the f-file against the queen on f3; White’s h-pawn capture leaves the threat unanswered. Black’s pawn later promotes on g1 with check.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: Black’s f-pawn has left the f-file. The black rook on f8 now sees down toward the queen on f3, with our pawn on h3 able to capture the pawn on g4.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: The pawn takes on g4. The next move is ...Rxf3. My file needed attention while everyone was watching the capture.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: The pawn becomes a queen with check. Two moves later, that new queen finishes on f2.

games.title: Alexander reaches the seventh rank
games.capsule: The a-pawn advances to a6 and captures on b7. Black’s coordinated rooks then outlast White’s remaining pieces.

beats.speaker: Alexander Aaronson
beats.text: I reach b7 by capture. This is a real promotion threat, and it deserves a look before the rooks arrive.

beats.speaker: Castle Andora
beats.text: The rook takes on a7; the knight on c6 can take that rook. The passer’s story and the rook’s safety are intertwined.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: After all the rook checks and the long walk, a pawn supplies the final checkmate on h6.

games.title: The king’s early night walk
games.capsule: Black’s king moves on turns two and four. The queen is later offered on a4, and White finishes with Qxd7#.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: The night is young. So is my development. I leave e8 before a knight or bishop has moved.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: I arrive on a4, where White’s queen on d4 can take me across the fourth rank. The board contains a clear invitation.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: White takes the bishop on d7 with mate. The queen offer created no recorded escape for the king on d8.

games.title: The queen practices teleportation
games.capsule: Four trips between c2 and d1 leave the rest of White’s position behind. A later queen visit to h5 meets ...Bg4+ and ...Bxh5.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: I have now made four round trips between d1 and c2. The teleportation department reports excellent attendance and no new territory.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The bishop check from g4 also attacks the queen on h5. The king has to answer the check, then ...Bxh5 follows in the recorded line.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: Black’s queen finishes the king’s walk on a4. A journey can be memorable and still end exactly where the score says.

games.title: The rook nearly gets away
games.capsule: A queen exchange opens the a-file rook adventure. After Ra8+, the rook visits a7, b7 and c7; Black takes it on c7.

beats.speaker: Castle Andora
beats.text: Check on the eighth rank! The queens have traded, and a rook has found a real line into the position.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: The rook has taken on b7 and can still retreat. Before another capture, find the enemy king’s reach.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The rook takes c7 with check. Black can answer Kxc7. At the previous position the scan prefers 26.Ra7, keeping the rook.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: Black wins on time after ...Ra8. This chapter is a useful comparison between an active rook and an expendable rook.

games.title: Dilorias goes through the front door
games.capsule: The queen takes the bishop on c1 with check and is taken by a rook. White’s queen and bishops then build the finishing net.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The bishop takes the pawn on f3, and White’s queen recaptures. Count that bishop before budgeting the queen’s later entrance.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: I take the bishop on c1 with check. The rook on a1 can reach c1 through b1. The front door is impressively well staffed.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The queen has been exchanged for a bishop. There is no second enemy queen being collected in reply.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: White’s f-rook gives mate on e1 after the black king’s long walk. Checks helped the story move, but did not restore the missing queen.

games.title: The midnight king wins on time
games.capsule: Ethelheim tours the board, survives, trades queens late and wins on the clock. The final ...c4 leaves a knight hanging on g8.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: e8–e7–e6–d6–c5. Five squares, no luggage. I am touring the position while the attacking pieces try to meet me there.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: The king takes the bishop on a7. This is not an empty walk: the board has offered captures along the route.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The queens have just exchanged on e6. This is an ordinary exchange, not one of the fifteen queen-for-material departures.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: Black wins on time here. The board still matters for review: White could take the knight on g8 with Nxg8. Our deeper check preferred 32...Nxh6 before this move.

games.title: Castling does not teleport a queen
games.capsule: The queen stays on d2 while Black’s pawn reaches e3. Castling long then allows that pawn to take the queen with check.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The black pawn reaches e3. It attacks d2, where the queen still stands. The threat is one diagonal step away.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: The king and rook castle. I remain on d2. The audience may now inspect the small pawn that has booked my seat.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: The pawn takes the queen with check. Castling moved two pieces, but neither was the attacked queen.

beats.speaker: King Ethelheim
beats.text: My walk ends on a4, with the black queen mating from b4. The crucial question was already visible on d2.

games.title: The Force gets a knight-shaped warning
games.capsule: The mirror opening becomes an active king hunt. The queen reaches g3, but ...Rg6 after Nf1 leaves her in the knight’s reach.

beats.speaker: Emanuel
beats.text: The earlier ...c4+ opened a queen check and attacked the bishop. Now ...cxb3 collects that bishop. There is real tactical counterplay in the king hunt; keep that resource in the story.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: I reach g3. The rooks are preparing their entrance, the king hunt is noisy, and I am still a piece that can be taken.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: The knight on f1 attacks g3. Black has a bishop on a6 that can capture this knight along a6–b5–c4–d3–e2–f1. The deeper recheck chooses ...Bxf1.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The rook joins the attack while the knight is still aiming at the queen. One more attacker did not remove that defender.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: Smoke bomb! A knight has collected me. The Force would like to amend the choreography before we add another rook.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: The PGN ends with White winning on time after Qe6. The queen sacrifice did not produce a recorded mating finish.

games.title: The rook brings back the opposing queen
games.capsule: Dilorias gives herself for the f3 knight. On move sixteen the c8 rook captures White’s queen with check. The recovery is real; the final win still belongs to White.

beats.speaker: Queen Dilorias
beats.text: I take the knight on f3. A pawn can take me, and the recorded reply is exf3. This is the evening’s queen-sac theme in miniature.

beats.speaker: Tara
beats.text: The queen is gone, and White’s e-pawn is now on f3. When reviewing a sacrifice, keep following the other pieces instead of ending the story here.

beats.speaker: Dasha
beats.text: Look down the c-file from the rook on c8: c7, c6, c5 and c4 are empty, and White’s queen is on c3. The rook can take it with check.

beats.speaker: Castle Andora
beats.text: The queen is collected on c3! A rook can make a dramatic entrance without inventing a new movement rule.

beats.speaker: Michael
beats.text: The knight has also been traded on d7. The resulting material is still not an equal refund: White retains a bishop alongside the rook.

beats.speaker: Glover
beats.text: White promotes the f-pawn and eventually mates on g2. We keep the excellent c-file discovery, and we keep the exact result. Both belong to the night.

checkpoints.title: The c-file opens
checkpoints.question: Black to move. Which checking move collects the queen on c3?
checkpoints.explanation: Rxc3+ takes White’s queen with check. The c-file is clear. White can answer bxc3, so the rook is part of the price; this is a real recovery, not a free queen.

checkpoints.title: Use the knight-shaped Force
checkpoints.question: Black to move. Which knight check forks the king and queen?
checkpoints.explanation: The knight lands on f3 with check against e1 and attacks the queen on d4. Ke2 Nxd4+ is one legal illustration, not the only possible king response. This is an unplayed analysis branch.

checkpoints.title: A queen offer can be accepted
checkpoints.question: White to move. Which move directly captures Black’s offered queen?
checkpoints.explanation: White’s queen can take the black queen on d3 along the open d-file. The recorded game instead continued Nf3 Qxd1+, and Manny won. This is an unplayed analysis branch.
